body.objective: Extend the compact Science Forge coordinator overview with evidence-based work-duration and queue-depletion forecasts, so a high-velocity multi-agent programme can restock each stream before its resident worker becomes idle. The forecast must be derived from append-only lifecycle, lease, report and request events rather than subjective percentage estimates or language-model guesses.
body.stop_condition: Land a documented forecasting section in `s-f overview` (or a tightly integrated read-only companion) with: (1) exact lifecycle statistics per stream and globally, including terminal-item count, DONE/OBSTRUCTED/SHORTFALL rates, calendar cycle time from first ACTIVE to terminal transition, summed live-lease active time, blocked/wait time where observable, and throughput over explicit deterministic windows; (2) robust duration summaries using median plus p20/p80 or p10/p90 empirical intervals, sample count and censoring count, never only a mean; (3) correct folding of multiple ACTIVE/READY/BLOCKED intervals, renewals, yields, aborts, expired leases, reopened items and concurrent or invalid overlapping leases, with invalid histories emitted as health findings rather than silently included; (4) a conditional remaining-time estimate for the active item based on elapsed active time and the empirical survival distribution, clearly labeled as a forecast; (5) a serial queue-depletion forecast in exact work-pull order for each resident stream, reporting earliest/median/conservative drain times, probability or empirical fraction of draining within caller-selected horizons, and a `RESTOCK_BY` time derived from a configurable safety quantile and lead time; (6) explicit `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` when the comparable terminal sample is below a documented threshold, with no fabricated ETA; (7) optional declared work-size or complexity classes in the work-item schema so estimates can stratify by comparable proof/certificate jobs, while preserving an unstratified fallback and forbidding automatic classification from prose or embeddings; (8) separate timing distributions by terminal disposition because exact obstructions may close much faster than constructive theorems; (9) `--forecast`, `--window <N|duration>`, `--horizon <duration>`, `--safety-quantile`, `--lead-time`, `--stream`, and versioned byte-stable `--json` output under explicit `--now`; (10) a compact coordinator display such as `active age | p50 remaining | ready depth | p50/p80 drain | restock by | n`; (11) deterministic fixtures for a healthy serial stream, insufficient data, censored active item, yield/resume, blocked wait, expired lease, overlapping-lease defect, fast obstruction-heavy stream, mixed complexity classes and a queue whose conservative drain precedes the required planning lead time; and (12) a benchmark showing the forecast reuses the single folded-state pass and does not materially regress the SF8 fast-overview target.
body.forbid: no claim that the forecast is a scientific completion date; no single-point ETA without interval and sample size; no use of wall-clock time not supplied through `--now`; no treating lease duration as verified CPU time; no counting blocked or expired time as active work without a separate label; no silent exclusion of censored, reopened or malformed histories; no assuming every work item is exchangeable across streams or complexity classes; no embeddings, LLM judgment or filename heuristics to infer complexity; no lifecycle transition, lease acquisition, queue mutation, automatic work generation, process kill, terminal-title change or git write; no coordinator alert that presents uncommitted files or live OS processes as authoritative completed results.
notes: Primary operational question: At the current empirical completion rate, when must the coordinator add another pullable proof-first item so the resident agent has no idle gap?

Use survival-style conditional remaining-time estimates rather than subtracting elapsed time from the unconditional median; long-running active items have already survived the short-duration portion of the distribution.

For a one-agent serial stream, queue drain is the convolution or empirical bootstrap of the active residual duration and the ordered ready-item durations. Exact closed-form sophistication is not required initially, but uncertainty must widen rather than disappear when data are sparse.

The first consumer has seven streams and enough append-only history to begin reporting descriptive statistics now. Forecast eligibility should remain fail-closed until each stratum reaches the documented sample threshold.

Live dashboard acceptance on 2026-07-20 exposed a necessary distinction between immediate pull depth and dependency-gated successor depth. Classical, observer and quantum-qme each showed DRAIN at ready depth one even though each also had an active item and a declared downstream chain that would unlock after terminal producer outcomes. The forecast must display both quantities separately: only currently pullable READY work counts as immediate reserve, while dependency-gated successors are a typed contingent runway with their unresolved producers and dependency modes shown. Contingent work must never be counted as pullable or used to fabricate a drain time, but its presence should let the coordinator distinguish a truly empty roadmap from a temporarily gated pipeline.
A later resource overlay may correlate duration with CPU, memory and disk receipts, but this request is lifecycle forecasting only. Resource measurements must remain separately typed.
